Playbook (accumulated from past tasks):
## strategies
[ace-0001] helpful=1 harmful=0 :: Before implementing a new function, read the existing module and its money/rounding helpers (e.g. ZERO, to_money, round_money) and reuse them so new code matches the project's established Decimal and rounding conventions.
[ace-0002] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: For weighted-average or division logic, guard against a zero denominator (e.g. empty lines / total quantity of zero) and return the module's zero constant rather than dividing by zero.
[ace-0004] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: When validating an integer parameter, reject bool explicitly (isinstance(x, bool)) before the int check, since bool is a subclass of int and True/False would otherwise pass as 1/0.
[ace-0005] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: Mirror existing error codes and message formats from sibling modules (e.g. reuse 'invalid_state' with the same f-string as issue_invoice/payments) so new validation is consistent with the project's BillingError conventions.
## common_mistakes
[ace-0003] helpful=1 harmful=0 :: When summing Decimal values, pass an explicit start value (e.g. sum(..., ZERO)) instead of relying on the default int 0, to keep types consistent and avoid mixing int and Decimal.
[ace-0006] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: Don't assume to_money/round_money accepts arbitrary input silently; verify how it handles floats, NaN, and non-Decimal types, and rely on its existing error (e.g. 'float_amount') rather than duplicating type checks.

item.content: When implementing a function that mirrors an existing sibling (e.g. next_renewal vs current_period), read the sibling first and reuse its exact arithmetic pattern (ensure_utc on inputs, timedelta(days=period_days), floor-division n = (delta // length)) so edge cases like before-start and exact-boundary align with established behavior.

For 'first X strictly after t' queries, compute n = (t - start) // length + 1 and return start + n*length; handle t < start separately by returning start + length, since floor division on negative deltas would otherwise give the wrong period.

Don't assume a datetime is timezone-aware or valid; route inputs through the project's ensure_utc helper so naive/non-datetime values raise the standard BillingError codes (naive_datetime/invalid_datetime) instead of failing with raw TypeError/ValueError.
